Alert.title: Alert
Alert.description: Represents an alert submitted by a user or verified by an admin.

description.description: Detailed description of the incident or alert.

category.description: Category of the alert (e.g., Security, Road, Power, Water, Health, Other).

location.description: Location of the incident (neighborhood/area in Goma).

status.description: Status of the alert (pending, verified, archived).

isAnonymous.description: Indicates if the alert was submitted anonymously.

createdAt.description: Timestamp of when the alert was created.

verifiedAt.description: Timestamp of when the alert was verified by an admin.

verifiedBy.description: Reference to AdminUser who verified the alert. (Relationship: AdminUser 1:N Alert)

AdminUser.title: AdminUser
AdminUser.description: Represents an administrator user with access to the admin dashboard.

id.description: Unique identifier for the admin user.

email.description: Email address of the admin user.

name.description: Full name of the admin user.

role.description: Role of the admin user (e.g., superadmin, editor).

definition.description: Collection of alerts. Includes fields like title, description, category, location, status, isAnonymous, createdAt, verifiedAt, and verifiedBy.  The 'verifiedBy' field contains the AdminUser ID, enabling direct authorization checks.
Collection of admin users. Used to store admin user profiles and their roles.

params.name: adminUserId
params.description: Unique identifier for the admin user.

firestore.reasoning: The Firestore structure prioritizes authorization independence and QAPs (Query According to Permissions). It separates public and admin data, using path-based ownership for user-submitted alerts and a dedicated collection for admin roles. The `Alert` documents include a `verifiedBy` field which explicitly represents the AdminUser that verifies an alert. The structure uses structural segregation, separating public alerts (available to all) from the potential drafts or admin-only data related to alerts. This avoids mixing data with different access needs in the same collection. By avoiding complex hierarchical authorization, the design enables more straightforward and auditable security rules. This structure also supports QAPs by allowing listing of only 'verified' alerts for public users, and all alerts for admin users, without using rules as filters.
